# recipe-box

## Project overview

Web app where families save, organize and share recipes.

Users: Non-technical family members, mostly on mobile.

Core features:
- Save recipes with photos and ingredients
- Share a recipe with family or publicly

Out of scope, do not build:
- Meal planning and shopping lists (later)

## Language policy

- Code, comments, docs and commit messages: English.
- Replies to the user: Italian.

## Tech stack

Uses: TypeScript, Next.js, Node.js, pnpm, PostgreSQL, Vitest, next-intl.

- Use the App Router in `app/`. Pages and layouts are Server Components; add `'use client'` only to components that need state, effects or browser APIs. Expose an environment variable to the browser only through the `NEXT_PUBLIC_` prefix, and never for a secret. Why: Server Components keep secrets and data fetching on the server and send less JavaScript to the browser.
- Use the Node.js version pinned in `.nvmrc` or in the `engines` field of package.json, never whatever version is installed globally. Why: Node.js versions differ in behavior and break native dependencies.
- Use pnpm for every install and script. Never run npm or yarn. Why: Mixing package managers creates conflicting lockfiles.
- Change the schema only through migration files committed with the code; never alter tables by hand. Pass values as query parameters, never by concatenating them into SQL. Why: Migrations rebuild the same schema in every environment, and parameters prevent SQL injection.

## Commands

- Dev: `pnpm dev`
- Build: `pnpm build`
- Test: `pnpm test`
- Lint: `pnpm lint`

## Code style

- Keep `strict` enabled in tsconfig.json. Never use `any`; use `unknown` and narrow it. Why: Strict types catch errors at compile time, and `any` silently turns the checks off.
- Read every user-facing string through next-intl: `useTranslations` in Client Components and `await getTranslations()` in async Server Components. Keep messages in one JSON file per locale under `messages/`, such as `messages/en.json`. Why: One API on both sides of the server boundary keeps every string translatable.
- App locales: en (default), it and es. Translate new text into every locale yourself.

## Testing

- Run tests with `vitest run`; plain `vitest` starts watch mode in an interactive terminal and never exits. Put each test file next to the code it tests, named `*.test.ts` or `*.test.js`. Why: A watch-mode run blocks the shell until someone stops it.

## Git workflow

- Write commit messages as Conventional Commits: `type(scope): description`, with types such as feat, fix, docs, test and chore. Mark a breaking change with `!` before the colon or a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer. Why: Typed messages make the history easy to scan and let tools derive changelogs and versions.

## Safety rules

- Never edit, skip or delete an existing test to make it pass. Fix the code, or stop and ask. Why: A passing test suite is only meaningful if the tests stay honest.
- Never run destructive commands without asking first, such as `rm -rf`, `git reset --hard`, `git push --force`, `git clean -f` or deleting a branch. Propose a reversible alternative when one exists. Why: These commands destroy work that neither git nor the file system can bring back.

## Domain notes

Private recipes never appear in search results.

- Store all quantities in metric units; convert only for display. Why: Keeps scaling and conversion logic in one place.

- Before adding a feature, read docs/PRODUCT.md.
